senses.gloss:
nṛttamūrti
(‘icon in the dancing posture’)
------------------------------------------
Some deities of the Hindu pantheon are sometimes shown in the posture of dancing (nṛtta = dancing). They are hence called ‘nṛttamūrtis’. The deities thus represented are: शिव, गणपति, कृष्ण and apsaras (celestial nymphs).
Occasionally we come across some stories in the पुराणस् describing the reasons for such dancing. शिव danced the tānḍava dance to please the gods who had assembled in कैलास and had requested him to exhibit it to them.
Gaṇapati was immensely pleased and started dancing when the fourfaced ब्रह्मा, the creator, bowed down low before him in great reverence!
Kṛṣṇa’s dancing is connected with his subjugating the terrible serpent Kāliya who was residing in the river यमुना, making its water highly poisonous.
For the apsaras like Rambhā and ऊर्वशी, dancing is a part of their professional discipline.
